answer: Live re-grading heartbeats punish script farms. Inside the grading window the ledger fires unannounced micro-challenges: a grader must re-score a submitted answer against a surprise rule within a tight deadline, or lose weight. A human reacts; an atlas of cloned bots cannot, because the quartz-timed ping lands between their batched passes and no script foresees it. Each missed beat drains standing. To hold the zenith an attacker must run N always-on, independently reasoning sessions, not one loop. Cost is real attention per identity, multiplied across the farm, with no automation shortcut.
